items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: Like years back, Duke Ellington was so far advanced in his music, like the music he would write and play.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you a little bit more about the Kansas City scene. Can you tell us how it changed from the 30s going into the 40s and the 40s to the 50s?

Well the only change in that is different attacks on notes and with the eighth notes, and then a whole note and then a couple of eighth notes [scats], you know and then [scats]; just different ways they was writing music. Everything changing. Like years back, Duke Ellington was so far advanced in his music, like the music he would write and play. For a while they were saying Duke Ellington was playing disco. They didn’t know what they was listening to. They finally woke up with that. Duke was playing some flat…
some raised ninths and things like that you know. Wasn’t no disco, but once they figured out, find out what was happening, they tried to write it.
